name: Resting in the Two Turning Points of the Breath

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: ūrdhve prāṇo hy adho jīvo visargātmā paroccaret | utpattidvitayasthāne bharaṇād bharitā sthitiḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: Bhairava answers: the supreme power, whose nature is to pour itself out (visarga), keeps sounding as the breath: prāṇa moving upward and out, jīva moving downward and in. By filling with awareness the two places where these movements arise, one comes to rest in fullness (bharitā sthitiḥ).
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh's notes (following the Kashmir Shaiva commentators) place the two points at the heart-centre, where the in-breath ends, and the outer dvādaśānta, about twelve finger-widths in front of the nose, where the out-breath ends. The verse itself only says 'the two places of arising'.
dharana.technique_name: Resting in the Two Turning Points of the Breath

checked_against: Lakshmanjoo lineage: repose.ghost.io (a site presenting Lakshmanjoo's 112 meditations) labels verse 24 as meditation 1; not checked in a print Lakshmanjoo edition.
GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y1 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 24 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: outer turning point: about twelve finger-widths in front of the nose (commentarial, 'outer dvādaśānta')
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The dharana's own map is two points joined by the path of the breath: the inner point where the in-breath ends and the outer point where the out-breath ends. The exact locations come from commentary (Singh's notes), not from the verse.
geometry.svg_hint: one dot at the heart, one dot in space in front of the nose, a soft arrow going out and coming back between them
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Settle into fullness
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention that was bouncing outward settles where the breath turns, and the pause is felt as full rather than empty. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally turns: inside at the end of the in-breath, outside at the end of the out-breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. If counting helps, an even four in and four out; otherwise do not count. No forced hold. Notice the natural brief turn at the top and bottom of each breath.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward the two turning points, not toward the air itself
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely so that no effort competes with the breath
orientation.gaze: Eyes lightly closed, or open and resting softly on the floor
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The two places where the breath turns: inside (heart-centre) and outside (space in front of the nose)
attention.secondary: The fullness of the pause itself

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Bhairava answers: the supreme power, whose nature is to pour itself out (visarga), keeps sounding as the breath: prāṇa moving upward and out, jīva moving downward and in. By filling with awareness the two places where these movements arise, one comes to rest in fullness (bharitā sthitiḥ).
adiyogi.method_summary: Breathe naturally. At the end of each in-breath, rest awareness for a moment at the inner turning point; at the end of each out-breath, rest it at the outer turning point. Do not stop, slow or lengthen the breath; meet the pause that is already there.

honesty.disclosure: Door 001 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 1 (verse 24) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 001 is dharana 1, verse 24. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture] and VBT method are linked by the School of 112 Doorways as a teaching device (Door 001 with dharana 001). It is not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Supportive resonance only: [retired posture] stillness makes the two breath-turn points easier to notice. Pairing remains school_device by door index.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Never hold or stop the breath for this door. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: If standing is not available, practice the same breath-turn attention seated upright in an open seat ([retired posture] or chair).
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Soften the knees if locking bothers them. Sit or hold a wall if balance or fatigue appear.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 001: the two turning points of the breath. It is the first dharana of the Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra, verse 24.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit, lie down, or stand, whatever is easiest. The map is two points: where the in-breath ends inside, near the heart, and where the out-breath ends outside, in front of the nose.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes soft or closed. Turn attention toward the turning points, not toward the air.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Breathe naturally. If counting helps, four in, four out, six easy rounds. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Rest at the inner turn after each in-breath, and at the outer turn after each out-breath. Notice the pause that is already there.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: scattered charge settles into fullness. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 24: fill the two places where the breath arises with awareness, and rest in fullness. Do not stop the breath. Meet the pause that is already there.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Take one free breath without watching it. Open the eyes. Carry the sense of fullness into whatever comes next.
